Write the drive angular frequency as Omega in the derivation to distinguish it from the free damped frequency omega_d. Use the printed Q_book=omega_d/(2 beta) convention; a separate Q 0 uses the natural frequency.

steps.explanation: The kinetic and elastic energies return to their initial values after one steady period, so friction work is the negative of input work.
Torque balance in phase and in quadrature determines both torsional stiffness and damping.
Use the inferred natural frequency rather than silently replacing it by the driving frequency.
An equivalent compact dimensionless expression makes the two conventions easy to compare.

checks: Friction work is nonpositive for the passive phase range 0<=alpha<=pi.
At a drive frequency equal to omega 0 the lag is pi/2; then D=Q 0 and Q_book=sqrt(D^2−1/4). At arbitrary phase D alone is not the quality factor.
limitations: The inferred stiffness must be positive and omega 0^2>beta^2 is required for the book decrement-based quality factor. Without a linear viscous damping law, steady work is determined but a free-decay quality factor need not follow from this one driven measurement.
When sin(alpha)=0 the dissipation vanishes and the finite-Q formulas become singular; interpret the ideal lossless limit separately.
